implementation_notes: Ruby layers accumulate as versions of the framework move on: Rails 6 hash-with-indifferent-access idioms beside Rails 7 keyword arguments, `delayed_job` beside `sidekiq`, ActiveRecord callbacks beside service objects for the same behaviour. Because the framework upgrades are the migrations and the framework keeps both APIs working for compatibility, the coexistence is explicitly supported and therefore permanent unless something forces it to end. The completion mechanism is a RuboCop cop banning the legacy API plus a task that counts remaining usages, so the migration has a visible number rather than an intention.
idiom_name: Rails 6 and Rails 7 idioms in one app; two background job adapters
code_sketch:
# rubocop: a cop is the completion mechanism
Metrics/MethodLength:
  Exclude: []
Style/HashSyntax:         # legacy form fails the build
  EnforcedShorthandSyntax: always
pitfalls: Framework upgrades that support both old and new APIs mean a migration is never forced to complete by the framework itself.
Two background job backends means two sets of retry semantics and two dashboards for one queue of work.
A gem pinning an old Rails version transitively can block the upgrade for every consumer of the shared library.
